name: Maya
context: Owns product, deployment, and customer support for a small Node.js service.
behavior: Skims first, acts only when impact is stated in plain language.
goal: Connect a repository and close the first reachable critical path.
friction: Extra overview and system pages delayed the first useful action.
lesson: Default directly to Feed and keep Review as the obvious next step.
result: Reached a verified record without needing security vocabulary.

name: Jon
context: Triages findings across twelve services during a normal workday.
behavior: Uses keyboard navigation and dismisses false positives quickly.
goal: Review the highest-impact item, inspect the patch, and assign ownership.
friction: Decorative counts and redundant status destinations competed with the queue.
lesson: Keep the queue dominant, retain j/k/Enter controls, and remove static navigation badges.
result: Completed triage with one primary action per row.

name: Priya
context: Arrives from an alert while monitoring several active incidents.
behavior: Needs freshness, severity, and state changes to be unambiguous.
goal: Confirm whether an observed attack reaches production code.
friction: Marketing-style success language weakened trust during an incident.
lesson: Use short operational confirmations and a single restrained success cue.
result: Verified the closed path with calm, explicit feedback.

name: Leo
context: Owns authentication and payment services in a TypeScript monorepo.
behavior: Distrusts broad rewrites and reads diffs before explanations.
goal: Validate that the proposed change is small and preserves login behavior.
friction: Three equally heavy AutoFix columns made the diff harder to locate.
lesson: Make the editor dominant and treat file scope and reasoning as supporting rails.
result: Located the changed control point immediately and prepared review.

name: Nina
context: Is handling her first security issue in a production repository.
behavior: Reads descriptions carefully and worries about making the wrong change.
goal: Understand why the finding matters and safely review the fix.
friction: Dense labels and multiple destination choices increased hesitation.
lesson: Use plain-language impact text and preserve a linear Feed-to-Review path.
result: Understood the public reachability and opened the correct patch.

name: Marcus
context: Reviews team risk before stand-up and delegates code ownership.
behavior: Needs a five-minute morning scan and clear ownership signals.
goal: Identify critical work and assign it without exploring the full platform.
friction: The workspace overview duplicated Feed without improving decisions.
lesson: Remove the redundant overview surface and make Feed the morning home.
result: Assigned the critical item and returned to the queue.

name: Elena
context: Checks exposure and evidence before an executive risk review.
behavior: Looks for consequence, ownership, and proof rather than code detail.
goal: Confirm that critical exposure is being closed and evidenced.
friction: System-health chrome looked like a product-completeness prop.
lesson: Keep health as a quiet persistent signal instead of a full navigation page.
result: Reached immunity records with the path and verification state intact.

name: Owen
context: Prepares evidence for a customer security review.
behavior: Follows structured proof and needs stable terminology.
goal: Trace a finding through change, replay, and evidence.
friction: Changing labels between product stages made the audit trail feel less reliable.
lesson: Keep Feed, AutoFix, and Immunity records named consistently everywhere.
result: Completed a coherent evidence chain.

name: Sam
context: Runs a repository scan while handling normal operational work.
behavior: Refuses workflows that block the screen during network operations.
goal: Start a scan, continue working, and receive completion feedback.
friction: Automatic navigation after a scan interrupted context.
lesson: Run scans in place, leave the workspace usable, and announce completion quietly.
result: The scan completed in the background without a blocking loader.

name: Aisha
context: Moves between repository, cloud, and container exposure.
behavior: Uses direct navigation and ignores ornamental summaries.
goal: Move from a cloud asset to the related code risk.
friction: Hard-coded sidebar counts looked stale and reduced confidence.
lesson: Remove static badges unless they are backed by live data.
result: Navigation stayed trustworthy and uncluttered.

name: Theo
context: Validates whether an exploit path has a practical code-level fix.
behavior: Moves quickly between attack validation and patch evidence.
goal: Open a pentest result, review the fix, and confirm replay closure.
friction: Celebratory motion would feel unserious after a security result.
lesson: Use a short check animation only after a completed action, with no bounce or confetti.
result: Received clear completion feedback without spectacle.

name: Grace
context: Evaluates Cefense using a public repository before connecting private code.
behavior: Needs a low-commitment path and transparent repository handling.
goal: Run a public scan and inspect a concrete finding.
friction: A forced full-screen loading state would look unsafe and slow.
lesson: Keep repository work visible and backgrounded; never replace the entire interface with a loader.
result: Completed evaluation while retaining context.

name: Ibrahim
context: Investigates a newly disclosed attack primitive and its variants.
behavior: Uses precise search and expects source context without marketing language.
goal: Find the matching code path and inspect the repair rationale.
friction: Repeated explanatory panels diluted the observed-to-code relationship.
lesson: Keep one queue, one selected finding, and one repair workbench.
result: Moved from intelligence to the selected code path directly.

name: Dana
context: Coordinates response to active authentication abuse.
behavior: Needs decisive prioritization and no surprise navigation.
goal: Open the critical item and confirm the exploit path is closed.
friction: A second dashboard and animated chrome slowed orientation.
lesson: Land on Feed, keep motion mechanical, and preserve the selected finding throughout.
result: Reached verified evidence with no detour.

name: Luis
context: Separates reachable reports from duplicate or non-actionable submissions.
behavior: Dismisses, assigns, and advances through a queue repeatedly.
goal: Clear findings with reliable feedback and stable selection.
friction: Silent dismiss actions made it unclear whether the queue had updated.
lesson: Confirm dismiss, pin, and owner changes in a restrained live-status message.
result: Cleared the queue without losing place.

name: Meera
context: Reviews payment and authentication risk under regulatory pressure.
behavior: Prioritizes minimal patches, ownership, and proof.
goal: Close a critical payment-path issue with reviewable evidence.
friction: Large red surfaces felt alarmist instead of operational.
lesson: Reserve red for severity and use quiet warm surfaces for the rest.
result: Reviewed the fix with clear consequence and low visual tension.

name: Chris
context: Coordinates remediation across a small team with strict change review.
behavior: Needs readable language and a predictable audit trail.
goal: Assign a finding, review a safe patch, and produce evidence.
friction: Tiny metadata and dense control clusters raised cognitive load.
lesson: Maintain the established type floor and group controls by task.
result: Completed the workflow without opening secondary tools.

name: Ravi
context: Evaluates whether a repair can be defended during formal review.
behavior: Avoids novelty and values explicit state language.
goal: Confirm the finding, patch scope, test, and evidence status.
friction: Demo-like metrics weakened the sense of a production instrument.
lesson: Remove hard-coded counts and redundant status pages.
result: The remaining surfaces read as operational records.

name: Sofia
context: Assesses how Cefense fits repository, cloud, and integration workflows.
behavior: Explores breadth but expects the core path to remain obvious.
goal: Inspect integrations, then verify the primary remediation loop.
friction: A catch-all System section obscured the distinction between core and supporting tools.
lesson: Rename the final group Workflow and keep only integrations and library there.
result: Explored platform breadth without losing the Feed anchor.

name: Ben
context: Evaluates product credibility, pricing, and operational proof.
behavior: Checks public pages first, then expects an obvious product experience.
goal: Understand the offer and reach a credible working flow.
friction: Too many app destinations looked like breadth added for a demo.
lesson: Keep core navigation primary and supporting tools visibly quieter.
result: Reached evidence without needing to understand every module.

name: Rachel
context: Reviews the company after opening a pitch deck.
behavior: Moves quickly from thesis to product proof.
goal: See a differentiated landing page and verify the product loop is real.
friction: A visible loading interstitial made the product feel staged.
lesson: Use no face-loading copy; preserve the prior surface while data resolves.
result: Reached the working fix flow without a presentation-like pause.

name: Ethan
context: Tests the product repeatedly and gives workflow feedback.
behavior: Notices small inconsistencies after repeated daily use.
goal: Review several findings without accumulating interaction fatigue.
friction: Repeated shadows, pulses, and active-state movement became tiring.
lesson: Keep motion short, static by default, and tied to completed actions only.
result: Repeated the flow without visual fatigue.

name: Hana
context: Checks regression coverage for a proposed security change.
behavior: Looks for exact state transitions and repeatable results.
goal: Confirm the replay test and evidence state update correctly.
friction: Ambiguous completion copy made it hard to distinguish prepared from verified.
lesson: Use distinct messages for review package ready and verification complete.
result: Observed clear, testable state changes.

name: Noah
context: Checks a repository finding while away from a full workstation.
behavior: Needs touch-safe controls and no horizontal page leaks.
goal: Open the top finding and understand the proposed fix.
friction: Wide workbench content can force horizontal movement on small screens.
lesson: Contain wide code inside its own surface and keep the page shell fixed.
result: Maintained a stable workstation shell on mobile.

name: Keiko
context: Owns Python services and package supply-chain risk.
behavior: Searches by package, file, or issue name before browsing.
goal: Find a supply-chain issue and review its reachable impact.
friction: Search competing with too many topbar controls reduced focus.
lesson: Keep search central and remove the low-value Docs action from the app header.
result: Found the relevant item with a single focused header.

name: Amir
context: Reviews agent and dependency risks in an AI service.
behavior: Needs concrete code impact rather than generic AI-security claims.
goal: Move from a relevant finding to an exact proposed change.
friction: Broad product language made the finding feel generic.
lesson: Keep file, line, reachability, and proposed code visible in the main path.
result: Reviewed a code-specific fix without extra explanation screens.

name: Victor
context: Manages repositories, containers, and CI integrations.
behavior: Switches scope often and expects the current repository to remain obvious.
goal: Run a scan and return to the prioritized queue without losing scope.
friction: Auto-redirecting on scan completion felt mechanical in the wrong way.
lesson: Keep scanning in the background and let the user decide when to open Feed.
result: Retained repository context and received completion confirmation.

name: Camila
context: Owns authentication UI and client-side session handling.
behavior: Responds to strong visual hierarchy but avoids dense consoles.
goal: Understand the critical session issue and inspect the fix.
friction: The critical card previously shouted louder than the information required.
lesson: Keep priority clear with typography and a restrained severity edge.
result: Found the critical item immediately without alarm fatigue.

name: Tom
context: Evaluates multiple clients and must explain findings clearly.
behavior: Moves between technical detail and executive proof.
goal: Review a repair and show a concise evidence record.
friction: Duplicate summary surfaces created different versions of the same story.
lesson: Use Feed as the only operational summary and reports as the proof endpoint.
result: Explained one coherent chain from risk to evidence.

name: Fatima
context: Triages findings for several customer environments.
behavior: Works quickly, repeats actions, and depends on scope clarity.
goal: Clear the current repository queue without confusing client context.
friction: Secondary counts and status surfaces increased scanning time.
lesson: Show scope once, remove redundant numbers, and keep secondary tools quiet.
result: Completed repeated queue work with lower cognitive load.

name: Martin
context: Reviews whether remediation claims are supported by a traceable record.
behavior: Reads evidence carefully and ignores most operational navigation.
goal: Open an immunity record and verify its source finding and replay result.
friction: A full System status page was unrelated to the evidence task.
lesson: Keep service health as a quiet persistent signal, not a competing destination.
result: Reached the record directly.

name: Zoe
context: Uses the public demo to learn how attack paths become code changes.
behavior: Explores examples and needs forgiving, self-explanatory actions.
goal: Open the demo, review a finding, and understand the patch.
friction: Enterprise-oriented labels made the first action feel high stakes.
lesson: Use direct verbs such as Connect, Review, Prepare, and Verify.
result: Completed the core path without training.

name: Aaron
context: Checks whether a customer-facing security issue is under control.
behavior: Needs a simple answer and avoids code-heavy areas.
goal: See whether critical exposure exists and whether it is resolved.
friction: The overview page repeated counts without answering what happens next.
lesson: Let Feed provide the answer and Immunity records provide proof.
result: Understood current risk and resolution state quickly.

name: Jules
context: Opens Cefense every morning before checking team messages.
behavior: Builds muscle memory and notices any inconsistent state or motion.
goal: Orient, clear the highest item, and leave within minutes.
friction: Novel animations and changing hierarchy become irritating with repetition.
lesson: Keep the shell still, transitions short, and success feedback transient.
result: Completed the morning loop predictably.

name: Wendy
context: Arrives from a referral with no product training.
behavior: Relies on labels and backs out when navigation feels crowded.
goal: Understand what Cefense does and reach a working result.
friction: Thirteen workspace destinations made the product look harder than it is.
lesson: Remove two redundant destinations and every static count badge.
result: Reached AutoFix with a smaller, clearer navigation system.

name: Dmitri
context: Lives in triage tools for hours and minimizes pointer use.
behavior: Uses j/k to move and Enter to act.
goal: Advance through findings without touching the mouse.
friction: Focus changes needed to remain visible without heavy outlines.
lesson: Retain keyboard controls and refined focus rings while removing hover movement.
result: Completed the primary path entirely from the keyboard.

name: Mina
context: Triages findings with assistive technology.
behavior: Depends on semantic controls, live regions, and stable headings.
goal: Select a finding and receive confirmation for each state change.
friction: Visual-only animation would not communicate completion.
lesson: Pair the restrained reward motion with an aria-live status message.
result: Received equivalent textual confirmation for every important action.

name: Joel
context: Works over an unstable connection and cannot tolerate blocking transitions.
behavior: Continues reading while network work completes.
goal: Start a repository scan without losing the current interface.
friction: Face-loading copy and screen replacement amplified perceived latency.
lesson: Use a null route fallback and in-place background progress messages.
result: The interface stayed available throughout long work.

name: Serena
context: Manages a large queue and is easily overloaded by secondary metadata.
behavior: Filters aggressively and pins only the items that matter now.
goal: Keep the current scope obvious and reduce the queue to critical work.
friction: Too many status numbers competed with the current repository and critical count.
lesson: Keep only critical, open, and updated status in the Feed header.
result: Oriented immediately and cleared the highest-priority item.

name: Malik
context: Opens Cefense during a high-pressure production incident.
behavior: Has low patience, high urgency, and zero tolerance for blocking UI.
goal: Confirm the finding, review the patch, and verify closure immediately.
friction: Any loader, redirect, or celebratory animation would interrupt response work.
lesson: Keep the app mechanical, preserve context, and limit reward motion to a 180ms check.
result: Completed the full path with no blocking screen or surprise transition.
